g.text: Fleet — Orchestration: the Router relays every hand-off (Executor / Operator / Supervisor never talk directly)

text.tspan: operators never talk to each other
One phase = the loop ①→⑥, and the Router is the only thing that touches the Operator and the Supervisor.
The Executor never talks to the Operator or Supervisor directly, and the Operator and Supervisor never talk to each other.
Think OSI: Executor / Operator / Supervisor are peers; the Router is the layer beneath that carries every message.
Multi-phase missions just repeat the loop — phase 2's operator works from phase 1's committed output, never from phase 1's operator. One operator per phase, always.

The commit is the SC's: after the Executor's report (⑥) the SC decides, and committing the verified phase is the SC's own act in the operator worktree — only the SC may make or grant that commit; the handler never commits there.

Before ①, the Executor always commits its own record (mission, state, prompt) in the handler repo, so the operator builds from committed state — a different commit, in a different repo, from the SC's phase commit above.

g.text: ① commit, then hand off phase
